wild dogs have a variable and short-lived effect on livestock numbers and are not always considered a pest by landholders.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the current best-practice approach to wild dog control in Australia has been unsuccessful.

the best-practice approach to wild dog control should be to prevent the ingress of wild dogs onto properties where they are a problem and not to undertake lethal control on properties where they are not causing losses.

the landscape-scale wild dog problem is best addressed by targeting lethal control to those producers most affected by wild dogs, while encouraging other producers and managers to adopt strategies that reduce the risk of dog ingress and to participate in coordinated lethal control programs.

best-practice wild-dog control should focus on preventing ingress of dogs onto properties troubled by predication and not on landscape-scale lethal control.
